key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in situ during CuInSe2 growth and enables high-voltage 1.0 eV bottom cells without heavy-alkali or Ag additions.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation route for tandem-ready chalcopyrite bottom cells, helping raise Voc while preserving low-bandgap absorber performance.
method: Formed GaOx by ion exchange during co-evaporation of the CuInSe2 absorber.
Compared conductivity/passivation effects under different Cu, Na, and oxygen-flow conditions.
Evaluated the resulting device performance in optimized CuInSe2 solar cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for the optimized device.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx behavior appears process-sensitive and partly crystalline, so reproducibility may depend on precise growth conditions and interface formation.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
